speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To begin our investigation, have you noticed if these lymph nodes are painful to the touch, or are they firm and painless?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those night sweats are "drenching," and you've lost twelve pounds in four weeks—that is a significant loss. Is the abdominal pain localized to a specific area, such as the right upper quadrant, or is it more generalized? Also, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits or appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of the nodes as "fixed" and painless, combined with your significant weight loss, night sweats, and drenching sweats, raises a high suspicion for lymphoma. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count. REQUEST TEST: LDH. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CTA_and_PET_CT.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT: White Blood Cells: Elevated; Hemoglobin: Slightly Decreased; Platelets: Normal. LACTATE DEHYDROGENASE: Elevated. IMAGING: CT Scan Thorax and Abdomen: Findings show massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. BIOPSY: Cervical Lymph Node: Findings reveal lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Patient
text: I have smoked about one pack a day for many years, and I drink socially. The abdominal discomfort and fatigue have both been getting worse. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma.

While your history of smoking and previous suggestion of tuberculosis are relevant, your presentation of painless, *fixed* supraclavicular nodes with drenching night sweats, significant weight loss, and worsening abdominal pain is highly specific for advanced lymphoma. I have already ordered a Complete Blood Count, LDH, Abdominal CTA, and a PET CT scan to confirm this diagnosis and stage the disease. Please wait for these results to be reviewed before considering any treatment for tuberculosis.
